paragraphs.zh: 补充情境：虚构读者还没听完项目问题，就为原方案辩解；另一位读者则快速拒绝了涉及隐私的提问。回应都很快，却不能据此认为目的或边界相同。先问清是在索取信息、作决定还是安排任务，不必为了改变类别而放弃必要立场。
paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader defends a project plan before hearing the full question; another quickly declines an intrusive private question. Both replies are fast, without establishing the same purpose or boundary. Distinguish seeking information, deciding and arranging tasks without abandoning a necessary position to alter a category.

paragraphs.zh: 可选讨论提示：“对方问了什么、读者回应了什么，哪些决定或信息尚未明确？”可以只读或讨论虚构人物，不需要提供个人事件、答案或计数。区分观察、解释及未知，允许不同理解和不参与；不以讨论结果要求继续谈话、披露信息或改变边界。
paragraphs.en: An optional discussion prompt asks: “What was asked and answered, and which decisions or information remain unclear?” Read alone or discuss the fictional reader without providing personal events, answers or counts. Separate observations, interpretations and unknowns. Different readings and nonparticipation remain available; discussion requires no continued conversation, disclosure or changed boundary.

paragraphs.zh: 新增情境和讨论提示由费马测试编辑部原创。成年人可自愿回想过去四周普通压力互动，不需寻找困难事件。十二条按四主题各三条整理；每条选择没有注意到、很少、有时、较常、经常或未计分。0至4只是类别标识，无点数或反向；没有机会、回想不清、不愿回答均保留未计分，不改成没有注意到。十二条都明确回应才整理私人记录；每主题六类计数合计三，并保留逐条陈述及所选类别。前两条选有时、末条未计分，表示两条陈述归入有时、一条未计分，不表示发生两次。相同计数可来自不同条目，不合总分、不求均值、不排名、不选主导反应或风险档。四篇完整指南在答题前、中途、全部未计分及结束后均可读。Pete Walker的4F和VA专业资料只是独立背景，不提供本题目、计分键、成因、诊断或验证；原创双语未建立常模、信效度或测量等值。类别不证明同意、生理、创伤经历、责任或未来行为。回答及记录只在页面内存，原有退出、重做、刷新、离开清除保持不变；不新增草稿、提交或分析。复制仅公开标题及入口，不含回答或计数。
paragraphs.en: FermatMind Editorial authored these additions. Adults may voluntarily recall ordinary pressured interactions over the past four weeks without seeking a difficult event. Twelve observations form four themes of three. Each enters Did not notice, Rarely, Sometimes, Often, Very often or Unscored. IDs 0–4 are category labels without points or reversals. No opportunity, unclear recall and withholding remain unscored rather than Did not notice. All twelve need explicit choices before a private record is organised. Six counts per theme add to three, preserving each statement and selected category. Sometimes for the first two and Unscored for the last means two statements categorised Sometimes, not two episodes. Equal counts can come from different items. There is no total, mean, ranking, dominant response or risk band. All four full guides remain readable before answering, midway, with all unscored and after completion. Pete Walker’s 4Fs and VA material provide separate background, not these items, scoring key, causes, diagnosis or validation. Norms, reliability, validity and measurement equivalence are unestablished for this original bilingual inventory. Categories establish no consent, physiology, trauma history, responsibility or future behaviour. Answers and records remain in page memory; existing exit, retake, reload and leaving clearing remain, without added drafts, submission or analytics. Copying includes only the public title and entry, without answers or counts.

paragraphs.zh: 补充情境：虚构读者离开自愿讨论以保留私人信息；另一人延后项目消息，之后发现交接未明确。距离、隐私选择与实际协作后果需要分别看。类别计数不能决定谁本该留下，也不产生恢复联系或解释离开原因的义务。
paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader leaves a voluntary discussion to keep information private; another postpones a project message and later finds an unclear handover. Distance, privacy choices and coordination outcomes differ. Counts decide neither who should have stayed nor any duty to resume contact or explain leaving.

paragraphs.zh: 补充情境：虚构读者在学习讨论中想提问，却找不到第一句话；另一人因为不愿披露隐私而选择沉默。外在都安静，但想回应而难开始与主动不答不同。三条观察不能判断冻僵、生理状态或原因，也不授权别人要求开口。
paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader wants to ask a study question but cannot find a first sentence; another stays silent to keep information private. Similar silence does not equate difficulty starting with a decision not to answer. Three observations determine no clinical freezing, physiology or cause and authorise no demand to speak.

paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader agrees to meet before checking caring responsibilities and later wants another time. The earlier reply, practical feasibility and current choice differ. A changed view proves no dishonesty and makes no earlier agreement permanent. Categories establish neither consent, an appeasing motive nor another person’s actual feelings.
